title: Open Source Is Dead. Long Live Open Source. — Saoud Rizwan, Cline
talk_summary: Cline's founder argues the open-source community layer is dying under AI-generated slop PRs and supply-chain risk, but open-weight models are commoditizing inference and will win on cost. His core practical claim: with good context, skills, rules, and verification gates, cheaper models (GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi) match frontier models at lower cost, and intelligence should live in the system around the model.

takeaways.technique: Route by cost-per-outcome, not raw intelligence
takeaways.what_they_do: They default to open-weight models (GLM/Kimi/DeepSeek) in an internal gateway and route work to the cheapest model that can do it, accepting more tokens for lower total cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: GLM used twice as many tokens but only cost half as much... GLM cleaned up dead code and verified that the build compiled before completing while Opus didn't.
takeaways.numbers: GLM: 2x tokens, half the cost, cleaned dead code, verified build; Opus: half the tool calls, faster, but left type errors and broke the production build. Coinbase: ~half AI spend cut with GLM/Kimi default.

takeaways.technique: Bake verification into the model's own loop
takeaways.what_they_do: They prefer models trained to spend tokens verifying their own output (compile, clean dead code) before declaring done, rather than relying on a separate reviewer to catch it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: GLM was trained to spend more tokens verifying its output... it's really the end result that matters.

takeaways.technique: Put intelligence in the system, not the model
takeaways.what_they_do: They invest in AI-native dev infrastructure — project skills, rules, verification systems, quality gates — so a mediocre model produces similar results to a smarter one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with the right AI native development infrastructure with project skills and rules... even a mediocre model can produce similar results as a more intelligent model

takeaways.technique: Internal LLM gateway as the cost-control point
takeaways.what_they_do: Companies standardize on an internal gateway that defaults to cheap open-weight models and routes for dollar efficiency, even at the cost of missing the newest closed-model features.
takeaways.numbers: ~50% AI spend cut while token usage grows (Coinbase, per speaker).

takeaways.technique: Treat third-party packages and agent-generated PRs as supply-chain risk
takeaways.what_they_do: They cite the litellm compromise (stolen PyPI tokens, credential harvester, RCE backdoor) and projects banning AI PRs; the lesson is to distrust third-party code and AI-generated contributions by default.

takeaways.technique: Don't over-invest in community/PR throughput you can't trust
takeaways.what_they_do: They observe big projects auto-closing all PRs and GitHub adding a disable-third-party-PRs switch because AI slop overwhelms review capacity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're automatically just closing all poll requests whether they're AI generated or not
